question: Deutchlander Machine Company (DMC) makes two types of printing presses: a four-color litho and a two-color litho. Demand for both products is booming and exceeds DMC's ability to satisfy it. Most raw materials are plentiful, but production is limited by three factors: a shortage of steel rollers, gear cutting capacity, and roller polishing capacity. Each four-color press requires 16 rollers, and each two-color press requires 8 rollers. The four-color presses require 30 hours of gear cutting and 8 hours of polishing time, and the two-color presses require 12 hours of gear cutting and 3 hours of polishing time. DMC is able to buy 100 rollers per week, and it has 160 hours of gear cutting time and 40 hours of polishing time available per week. To avoid harming long-term sales, DMC does not want to raise prices. At current prices DMC will earn a profit of DM24,000 on each four-color press made and DM10,000 on each two-color press made. So as not to abandon either product market, DMC also wants to produce at least two units of each press each week. Formulate DMC's problem as a linear program to maximize its profit.

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    # Products
    "products": ["four_color", "two_color"],

    # Profit per press (DM)
    # "DM24,000 on each four-color press" / "DM10,000 on each two-color press"
    "profit": {"four_color": 24000, "two_color": 10000},

    # Rollers required per press
    # "Each four-color press requires 16 rollers" / "two-color press requires 8 rollers"
    "rollers_per_press": {"four_color": 16, "two_color": 8},

    # Gear cutting hours required per press
    # "four-color presses require 30 hours of gear cutting" / "two-color ... 12 hours"
    "gear_hours_per_press": {"four_color": 30, "two_color": 12},

    # Polishing hours required per press
    # "four-color ... 8 hours of polishing" / "two-color ... 3 hours"
    "polish_hours_per_press": {"four_color": 8, "two_color": 3},

    # Resource availability per week
    # "able to buy 100 rollers per week"
    "rollers_available": 100,
    # "160 hours of gear cutting time ... per week"
    "gear_hours_available": 160,
    # "40 hours of polishing time available per week"
    "polish_hours_available": 40,

    # Minimum units of each press per week
    # "produce at least two units of each press each week"
    "min_units": 2,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Sets
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["products"])

    # Variables: integer number of presses (indivisible units)
    model.x = pyo.Var(
        model.P,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=(d["min_units"], None),
    )

    # Objective: maximize weekly profit
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["profit"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # Constraint: steel rollers
    def rollers_rule(m):
        return sum(d["rollers_per_press"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["rollers_available"]

    model.rollers = pyo.Constraint(rule=rollers_rule)

    # Constraint: gear cutting capacity
    def gear_rule(m):
        return sum(d["gear_hours_per_press"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["gear_hours_available"]

    model.gear = pyo.Constraint(rule=gear_rule)

    # Constraint: polishing capacity
    def polish_rule(m):
        return sum(d["polish_hours_per_press"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["polish_hours_available"]

    model.polish = pyo.Constraint(rule=polish_rule)

    return model
